population: the 3,764 forced-pairing tails of the universal-key re-key (suspect_list.jsonl, mark==forced-pairing)
method: each claimant position was resolved in the paired sources and the Isabelle command at that line read, giving four position classes: real declaration / locale interpretation instance / lemmas alias / none

residual_hazard_not_present_in_this_popu.what: a type-class internal name is theory-BASE-name qualified, thm128 hashes sorts but compute_constituents walks Const and Type only, so two same-named classes in same-base-named theories in DISJOINT cones would give one key to two different facts
residual_hazard_not_present_in_this_popu.why_it_cannot_hide_here: thm128 DOES hash TVar/TFree sorts, so a sort difference alone always splits the tail; a collision therefore needs identical sort STRINGS denoting different classes, which needs two same-base-named theories in disjoint cones; both facts would then be in the corpus dump and appear as two claimants, so claimants_in_mutually_disjoint_session_cones (142 keys, all inspected) is a complete test for this population -- modulo a partner dropped by the dump infra filter
residual_hazard_not_present_in_this_popu.verdict: all 22 are single-claimant Hoare_Time.Vars facts, monomorphic over com/aexp, with Hoare_Time.Vars in their constituent LONG names; no sort ambiguity in play

subpopulations.name: all_forced_pairing
subpopulations.query: row['mark']=='forced-pairing' in suspect_list.jsonl; the audited key is the one new entry with mark=='forced-pairing' (exactly one per row)

subpopulations.name: single_dump_record_no_name_choice
subpopulations.query: len(dump[new_key])==1 -- the key carries one dump record, so nothing about the name is chosen
subpopulations.note: 50.5% of the population: the 'which name' question is vacuous here; these are forced-pairing only because a SIBLING key on the same tail was already taken by B.0/B.1

subpopulations.name: multi_dump_record_name_chosen
subpopulations.query: len(dump[new_key])>1 -- several dump records (claimants) on the key, so choose_dump_record picks which name/position is recorded

subpopulations.name: relation_all_locale_interpretation_instances
subpopulations.query: len(claimants)>1 and every claimant position resolves to an interpretation/global_interpretation/sublocale command
subpopulations.note: one locale fact transported by several interpretations of the same locale; every claimant prints the term through its own interpretation's abbreviation, which is why 81 of these have differing prop STRINGS for one term

subpopulations.name: relation_lemmas_alias_of_a_real_declaration
subpopulations.query: len(claimants)>1 and claimant position classes == {alias, real}: one claimant is the lemma/definition site, another is a `lemmas`/`declare` re-export

subpopulations.name: relation_only_lemmas_aliases
subpopulations.query: len(claimants)>1 and every claimant position resolves to `lemmas`/`declare` (the proving site is not itself a claimant on this key)

subpopulations.name: relation_several_real_declarations_different_names
subpopulations.query: len(claimants)>1, all claimant positions are real declarations, claimant names differ: the same statement declared/generated twice (duplicated arity_theorem/fun/datatype, parallel theories)

subpopulations.name: relation_vendored_source_copies_same_name
subpopulations.query: len(claimants)>1, all claimant positions are real declarations, all claimant names identical: the same .thy text vendored into a second session (e.g. Van_Emde_Boas_Trees carries a private copy of Separation_Logic_Imperative_HOL)

subpopulations.name: relation_mixed_other
subpopulations.query: len(claimants)>1 and the claimant class set is none of the four above

subpopulations.name: name_is_a_real_declaration
subpopulations.query: the position of dump[new_key][picked] resolves to a lemma/theorem/definition/fun/datatype/inductive/arity_theorem/... command

subpopulations.name: name_is_a_locale_interpretation_instance
subpopulations.query: the position of dump[new_key][picked] resolves to interpretation/global_interpretation/sublocale
subpopulations.note: a true, citable name (Isabelle resolves it), but it names an INSTANCE, not the proving site

subpopulations.name: name_is_a_lemmas_alias
subpopulations.query: the position of dump[new_key][picked] resolves to `lemmas`/`declare`

subpopulations.name: name_has_no_resolvable_declaration_site
subpopulations.query: dump[new_key][picked] has no position, or its position resolves to no command

subpopulations.name: name_is_an_index_into_a_generated_or_lemmas_bundle
subpopulations.query: picked name matches r'\(\d+\)$' -- e.g. X.simps(385), X.distinct(5), Thy.r_defs(7); numbering fixed by the generating command / the `lemmas` line, stable across sessions

subpopulations.name: name_is_an_index_into_a_DYNAMIC_fact_collection
subpopulations.query: picked name is Thy.coll(n) where `coll` is declared `named_theorems` in theory Thy -- numbering depends on what is loaded, not stable across sessions
subpopulations.note: the only one: Heap_Monad.effect_elims(22); BOTH claimants on that key carry that same name, so no better name was available

subpopulations.name: dynamic_collection_name_present_but_avoided
subpopulations.query: some claimant name is Thy.coll(n) with coll a named_theorems of Thy, and the picked name is NOT that one
subpopulations.note: the old stored name pinned the real declaration in every one of these

subpopulations.name: non_real_name_picked_while_a_real_declaration_was_on_the_key
subpopulations.query: picked class != 'real' and some claimant class == 'real'
subpopulations.note: EMPTY: the pick never left a better name on the table

subpopulations.name: recorded_name_differs_from_the_old_stored_name
subpopulations.query: dump[new_key][picked].name != store[old_key].name
subpopulations.note: one key, single-claimant: the dump knows this fact only as Query.rr.lr_sets_ident, the store had the Measure_QuasiBorel_Adjunction.real_real.* interpretation instance name; both are true names of the same proposition

subpopulations.name: pick_marked_arbitrary
subpopulations.query: plan.pick_mark[new_key]=='arbitrary' (the name test did not single out one record)
subpopulations.note: 87 of 88 because every claimant carries the SAME name (so only position was at stake); the 88th had two of three claimants carrying the old name

subpopulations.name: position_gained_where_there_was_none
subpopulations.query: store[old_key].position is None and dump[new_key][picked].position is not None

subpopulations.name: position_points_at_a_lemmas_line_only_a_name_introduced
subpopulations.query: picked position resolves to `lemmas`/`declare`

subpopulations.name: position_points_at_an_interpretation_command
subpopulations.query: picked position resolves to interpretation/global_interpretation/sublocale
subpopulations.note: the instance is created there; the PROOF lives in the locale body, which is not a claimant on this key

subpopulations.name: position_regressed_from_a_declaration_to_an_alias_line
subpopulations.query: old position resolved to a real declaration or an interpretation command AND the picked position resolves to `lemmas`/`declare`/nothing
subpopulations.note: all 25 are interpretation-command -> `lemmas` line; old positions were written by backfill_positions (keyed by universal key alone) so they are not authoritative either

subpopulations.name: position_absent_after_migration
subpopulations.query: dump[new_key][picked].position is None

subpopulations.name: claimant_prop_strings_differ
subpopulations.query: len({r.prop for r in dump[new_key]})>1
subpopulations.note: all 248 verified as ONE term printed differently: 81 differ only in locale/abbreviation qualifiers, 167 in available notation (subst_cls C s vs C . s; nat vs omega; sats(A,p,e) vs A,e |= p; lambda vs %; line wrapping)

subpopulations.name: claimant_prop_strings_differ_qualifier_only
subpopulations.query: as above, and equal after stripping every `Ident.` qualifier

subpopulations.name: claimant_prop_strings_differ_notation_only
subpopulations.query: as above, and still different after stripping qualifiers

subpopulations.name: claimants_in_mutually_disjoint_session_cones
subpopulations.query: claimant sessions span >1 session and no claimant session's ROOT closure contains all the others -- the ONLY shape in which a base-name/type-class ambiguity could put two DIFFERENT facts on one key
subpopulations.note: 130 are the Isabelle/ZF Forcing/Transitive_Models/ZF-Constructible lineage (sep_rules/sep_rules'/nth_rules re-export bundles and duplicated arity_theorem/schematic_goal generations over ZF-Constructible's own theorems); 12 are vendored copies or parallel locale interpretations. Every one inspected: same statement. Isabelle/ZF has no type classes, so no sort ambiguity is even possible in the 130

subpopulations.name: claimants_share_one_theory_base_name
subpopulations.query: the claimant theories all have the same base name (different long names) -- fact names are byte-identical by construction there

subpopulations.name: vector_dropped_by_the_migration
subpopulations.query: row.new[i].vector_dropped -- name or prop diverged from the old record, so the embedded document text changed
subpopulations.note: 189 = 1 name divergence + 189 expr divergence (union); matches the run's vector_dropped flags exactly. These get re-embedded from the new text by _auto_embed, so no vector is left describing a name the record no longer has

subpopulations.name: picked_prop_printed_in_degraded_ascii_while_a_better_printing_was_available
subpopulations.query: picked prop matches ASCII surrogates (==> --> %x \< /\) and some other claimant's prop does not
subpopulations.note: EMPTY: measured over all 1,862 multi-claimant keys; 3 keys have every claimant printed with ASCII surrogates, so nothing better exists there

subpopulations.name: position_improved_from_an_alias_line_to_a_real_declaration
subpopulations.query: old position resolved to `lemmas`/`declare`/nothing AND the picked position resolves to a real declaration

subpopulations.name: position_points_at_a_real_declaration
subpopulations.query: picked position resolves to a lemma/theorem/definition/fun/datatype/inductive/arity_theorem/... command
